newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES DEPRESSED IN LIQUID MARKET.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES DEPRESSED IN LIQUID MARKET.

text.p: Zimbabwe's money market opened short on Tuesday with trading rates quoted firmer in quiet trade, dealers said.

"The market is a bit tight at the moment. There hasn't been any maturity of treasury bills today," a dealer said, adding that as a result the central Reserve Bank had not auctioned any bills as it normally does to mop up excess liquidity.
Discount houses were however selling the central bank paper on the secondary market at 15.75 percent and call money was also quoted at 15.75 percent, up from 15.50 the previous day.

NCDs redeemable after 30, 60 and 90 days were being bought at 16.50 from 16.35 percent and sold at 16.25 percent from 16 percent while bankers acceptance bills were at 16.25 amd 16 percent (buying and selling) from 16 and 15.75 percent on Monday.
Reserve Bank figures showed the market closed with a Z$28 million deficit on Monday from a previous surplus of Z$122.1 million.
